name: Asti
terms: Denominazione di Origine Controllata e Garantita, Italy's top tier. Stricter than DOC, and given only to wines that have been DOC for at least seven years.
Denominazione di Origine Controllata. The label names a precise area, and the wine is tested during production.
Indicazione Geografica Tipica, Italy's broad regional tier.
An aged Italian wine. Chianti Riserva needs at least 6 months in barrel and 3 more in bottle before release.
Asti is sweet, sparkling and low in alcohol, from Moscato Bianco. Moscato d'Asti is only lightly sparkling, with even less alcohol.

notes: Asti is a sweet, low-alcohol sparkling wine from Moscato Bianco, and Moscato d'Asti is only lightly sparkling and lower still in alcohol.
It is very floral, with peach and apricot flavors and the musky note of Muscat.
It has enough acidity to balance its sweetness.
It is best young, since after two years it loses its fresh, floral notes and turns heavier.

blurb.text: A DOCG for white wines from Moscato Bianco, grown in the hills of the Asti, Cuneo and Alessandria provinces of Piedmont. Asti spumante is fully sparkling and may be dry or sweet, while Moscato d'Asti is sweet, gently fizzy and low in alcohol. More than 90 million bottles were made in 2024.
